name: Kruger Mpumalanga International Airport
before:
The airport for Kruger National Park, 16 km from Mbombela as the crow flies and 27 km by road. It opened in October 2002, replacing the smaller Nelspruit Airport, and it exists mainly for safari traffic.

The terminal is the thing clients remember. It is almost entirely under a thatched roof covering around 7,350 square metres, which makes it the largest thatched structure in Africa.

Flights are to other South African cities and to regional destinations. A direct European link was tried between November 2022 and March 2023, when Discover Airlines flew from Frankfurt by way of Windhoek, but it was dropped for lack of demand.
after:
The airport for Kruger National Park, 16 km from Mbombela as the crow flies and 27 km by road.

What clients remember is the terminal. It sits under a thatched roof covering around 7,350 square metres, and the airport calls itself the largest thatch-constructed airport in the world.

Flights are to other South African cities and to regional destinations. A direct European link was tried between November 2022 and March 2023, when Eurowings Discover flew from Frankfurt by way of Windhoek, but it was dropped for lack of demand.

claims.claim: Eurowings Discover flew Frankfurt to the airport via Windhoek from November 2022 to March 2023, dropped for lack of demand
claims.inAfter: A direct European link was tried between November 2022 and March 2023, when Eurowings Discover flew from Frankfurt by way of Windhoek, but it was dropped for lack of demand.
claims.note: Was 'Discover Airlines'. Both reports name the airline as it was called at the time, Eurowings Discover (Tourism Update: 'Lufthansa's long-haul leisure brand'); Wikipedia calls it Discover Airlines. Tourism Update (February 2022) gave the first season as 15 November 2022 to 25 March 2023, three times a week via Windhoek; Aviation.Direct (17 March 2023) reported the flights, running since November 2022, suspended indefinitely for lack of demand, with no date to resume. The airport's current destination list has no European city.

claims.why: Wikipedia alone (21 October 2002). The operator's home, About, airline and development zone pages give no opening date; the only other source found, ABB's July 2001 release on the start of construction, expected the airport to be 'fully operational in the second half of 2002', a forecast rather than a record.

Wikipedia alone. OurAirports lists Nelspruit Airport (FANS) as a small airport without scheduled service, which does not by itself show that this airport replaced it, and no operator page mentions it.

claims.claim: about 315,000 passengers in 2024, and more than that in the first ten months of 2025
claims.why: Held back: a new fact that replaces nothing (the old text gives no traffic). The operator's monthly figures add up to 314,957 passengers in 2024, Wikipedia's infobox figure for 2024, against 255,176 in 2019; January to October 2025 add up to 318,919, already more than the whole of 2024 and about 24 per cent up on the same months of 2024.

claims.claim: FCDO: SANParks advises against the Kruger park's Numbi gate
claims.why: Held back: a warning that replaces nothing, but the one Andy may most want here. The FCDO's South Africa advice (updated 8 July 2026, still current 23 September 2026) says that after a violent attack killed a tourist in Kruger National Park, SANParks advises against using the Numbi gate, with protests and violent incidents on the R538 road leading to it, and that two local tourists were killed in a rare violent incident inside the park in May 2026 (suspects arrested). The FCDO does not say how far the gate is from this airport, and that was not checked. As an attributed line it could rest on the FCDO page alone: 'The FCDO says SANParks advises against using the park's Numbi gate.' SANParks' own site refused the link lister (403) and was not tried again.

sources.org: UK FCDO (Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office)
